name: Sky Woman
role: The woman who falls from the Sky World in Haudenosaunee creation accounts and becomes the first woman on the earth.
symbols: seeds of the Tree of Life
fun_fact: In a Mohawk telling, her head is placed in the night sky and she becomes Grandmother Moon, who keeps time and watches over the waters.

name: Turtle
role: The great turtle who offers his back as a place for the earth to grow, giving the land its Haudenosaunee name, Turtle Island.
fun_fact: Haudenosaunee teachers often point to the thirteen plates of a turtle's shell as a reminder of the thirteen moons of the year.

name: Water Spider
role: A small water being named among the divers in some Haudenosaunee creation tellings.
fun_fact: Different tellers name different divers, and Water Spider appears in some accounts of the earth's making while Muskrat takes that role in others.

name: Coyote
role: The Karuk trickster and culture hero who steals fire from the Yellow Jacket sisters and gives it to the people.
fun_fact: Coyote wins the fire by flattery, then marks the Yellow Jacket sisters with black coals, which is why yellow jackets are banded black and yellow.

name: Raven
role: The Tlingit trickster and transformer who steals the light from the chief at the head of the Nass River.
fun_fact: Raven is said to have been white until he was held in a smoke hole, and he is credited with teaching the Tlingit everything from canoe-making to halibut hooks.

name: White Buffalo Calf Woman
role: The Lakota sacred woman who brings the pipe and the seven ceremonies and promises to return.
fun_fact: Her Lakota name is Ptesan Win, and her departure is told as a promise: she will come again, and white buffalo calves are watched for as signs.

name: Changing Woman
role: The Diné woman of the seasons, mother of the Hero Twins, honoured in the Kinaaldá and the Blessingway.
fun_fact: Her Diné name, Asdzaa Nadleehe, means something like the woman who changes, and she is said to grow young again with each spring.

name: Monster Slayer
role: The elder Diné Hero Twin, son of the Sun, who clears the monsters from the world.
fun_fact: He is Naayee' Neizghani, and his brother Born for Water travels with him to find their father, the Sun, who tests them before giving them weapons.

name: Corn Mother
role: The woman in Wabanaki tradition whose body becomes the first corn, beans and squash.
fun_fact: In Penobscot tellings the first corn grows where her body touches the earth, and the people are told to work the ground and give thanks for it.

name: Gluskabe
role: The Wabanaki culture hero who travels the land making it ready for people and teaches them how to live.
fun_fact: Stories about Gluskabe are told across Wabanaki nations under different names, and he is often shown as clever, strong and a little too pleased with himself.
